# Lab 4 — SBOM Generation and Software Composition Analysis

## Task 1 — SBOM and CVE scan

Two SBOMs were generated from the same Juice Shop image, `bkimminich/juice-shop:v20.0.0`, using Syft: one in CycloneDX JSON format and one in SPDX JSON format.

| SBOM file | Format | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| `labs/lab4/juice-shop.cdx.json` | CycloneDX components | 3069 |
| `labs/lab4/juice-shop.spdx.json` | SPDX packages | 909 |

The CycloneDX `specVersion` is **1.7**.

CycloneDX reported 3069 components because its component list also included 2160 individual files, in addition to 907 libraries, one application, and one operating-system component. SPDX reported 909 packages, which matches the 909 non-file CycloneDX components, so the difference comes mainly from how the two formats represent and count the inventory rather than from discovering different software.

**Evidence — SBOM counts and CycloneDX spec version.**

<img alt="Task 1 evidence showing CycloneDX and SPDX SBOM counts and CycloneDX specVersion." src="data:image/png;base64," />

The CycloneDX SBOM was then scanned with Grype. Scanning the SBOM instead of the image separates inventory generation from vulnerability analysis: the same stored inventory can be rescanned later when vulnerability databases change, without pulling or rebuilding the original image.

The Grype scan found **189** vulnerability matches.

| Severity | Count |
|---|---:|
| Critical | 14 |
| High | 85 |
| Medium | 69 |
| Low | 14 |
| Negligible | 7 |
| **Total** | **189** |

**Evidence — Grype scan from SBOM and severity table.**

<img alt="Task 1 evidence showing Grype scan from the CycloneDX SBOM and severity counts." src="data:image/png;base64," />

Nine of the ten highest-ranked findings have a fix available. Since all ten are Critical, I would first prioritize the nine vulnerabilities with an available fixed version because they can be remediated immediately by upgrading the affected dependency; the remaining vulnerability without a listed fix would require mitigation, replacement, removal, or further risk analysis.

## Task 2 — Compare with an all-in-one scanner

Trivy was used as the all-in-one scanner against the same Juice Shop image, `bkimminich/juice-shop:v20.0.0`. Unlike the Grype step in Task 1, this scan inspected the image directly instead of consuming the CycloneDX SBOM file.

The severity comparison is:

| Severity | Grype from SBOM | Trivy image scan | Delta, Trivy - Grype |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Critical / CRITICAL | 14 | 11 | -3 |
| High / HIGH | 85 | 69 | -16 |
| Medium / MEDIUM | 69 | 78 | +9 |
| Low / LOW | 14 | 42 | +28 |
| Negligible | 7 | 0 | -7 |
| **Total** | **189** | **200** | **+11** |

The table normalizes severity names because Grype reports title-case severities such as `Critical`, while Trivy reports uppercase severities such as `CRITICAL`.

**Evidence — Trivy scan and severity counts.**

<img alt="Task 2 evidence showing Trivy image scan severity counts." src="data:image/png;base64," />

The tools also disagreed on individual identifiers. Grype reported 107 unique identifiers that did not appear in Trivy's result, while Trivy reported 114 unique identifiers that did not appear in Grype's result.

**Evidence — identifiers found by only one tool.**

<img alt="Task 2 evidence showing vulnerability identifiers found only by Grype or only by Trivy." src="data:image/png;base64," />

### Divergent identifiers

| Direction | Identifier | Package | Explanation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trivy-only | `CVE-2025-57349` | `messageformat@2.3.0` | Trivy reported this vulnerability using the GitHub Security Advisory npm database. The same npm package and version are present in the CycloneDX SBOM consumed by Grype, but Grype produced no matching vulnerability, so the difference is most likely caused by different advisory data or vulnerability-matching rules rather than package discovery. |
| Grype-only | `CVE-2026-48617` | `node@24.15.0` | Grype reported this vulnerability for the Node.js runtime and classified the artifact as a `binary`. Trivy's scan results catalog Debian OS packages and Node/npm language packages but do not expose the Node.js runtime as an equivalent binary component, so this difference is most likely caused by different component discovery or matching coverage between the scanners. |

**Evidence — Trivy-only case.**

<img alt="Task 2 evidence for the Trivy-only CVE-2025-57349 finding on messageformat." src="data:image/png;base64," />

**Evidence — Grype-only case.**

<img alt="Task 2 evidence for the Grype-only CVE-2026-48617 finding on the Node.js binary runtime." src="data:image/png;base64," />

The decoupled inventory approach is worth the extra moving part when the SBOM becomes a reusable artifact: the team can scan the same inventory again when vulnerability data changes, archive what was shipped, and use it later in Lab 8 as the predicate for a signed attestation. It is also useful when different teams or tools need to consume the same software inventory without pulling the original image again. A single binary scanner such as Trivy is the better answer when the goal is a fast operational check of one image with fewer files and less process overhead. In practice, the SBOM approach gives stronger traceability, while the all-in-one scanner is simpler for quick feedback.

## Bonus — A sign-ready attestation

The sign-ready attestation was created as `labs/lab4/juice-shop-attestation.json`. This file is only the in-toto statement/envelope for the existing CycloneDX SBOM; it is not signed yet. Lab 8 will handle signing.

The image repository digest used for the subject was:

```text
bkimminich/juice-shop@sha256:fd58bdc9745416afce8184ee0666278a436574633ea7880365153a63bfd418b0
```

The SHA-256 value written into `subject[0].digest.sha256` was:

```text
fd58bdc9745416afce8184ee0666278a436574633ea7880365153a63bfd418b0
```

The attestation was generated with this `jq` command:

```bash
jq --arg stmt_type "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v0.1" \
   --arg image "bkimminich/juice-shop:v20.0.0" \
   --arg digest "fd58bdc9745416afce8184ee0666278a436574633ea7880365153a63bfd418b0" \
   --arg predicate_type "https://cyclonedx.org/bom" \
   '{
      _type: $stmt_type,
      subject: [
        {
          name: $image,
          digest: {
            sha256: $digest
          }
        }
      ],
      predicateType: $predicate_type,
      predicate: .
    }' \
   labs/lab4/juice-shop.cdx.json \
   > labs/lab4/juice-shop-attestation.json
```

The first 20 lines of the generated file are:

```json
{
  "_type": "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v0.1",
  "subject": [
    {
      "name": "bkimminich/juice-shop:v20.0.0",
      "digest": {
        "sha256": "fd58bdc9745416afce8184ee0666278a436574633ea7880365153a63bfd418b0"
      }
    }
  ],
  "predicateType": "https://cyclonedx.org/bom",
  "predicate": {
    "$schema": "http://cyclonedx.org/schema/bom-1.7.schema.json",
    "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
    "specVersion": "1.7",
    "serialNumber": "urn:uuid:69bd5f2a-5ca6-4d2b-bbf9-01d5f91dedca",
    "version": 1,
    "metadata": {
      "timestamp": "2026-09-30T05:45:36Z",
      "tools": {
```

The top-level validation output was:

```json
{
  "_type": "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v0.1",
  "subject": [
    {
      "name": "bkimminich/juice-shop:v20.0.0",
      "digest": {
        "sha256": "fd58bdc9745416afce8184ee0666278a436574633ea7880365153a63bfd418b0"
      }
    }
  ],
  "predicateType": "https://cyclonedx.org/bom",
  "predicateBomFormat": "CycloneDX",
  "predicateSpecVersion": "1.7"
}
```

The digest is used instead of only the tag because a tag such as `v20.0.0` can be moved to another image, while the digest identifies the exact image content that this SBOM describes.

This file claims that the CycloneDX SBOM in the `predicate` describes the image subject `bkimminich/juice-shop:v20.0.0` at the listed SHA-256 digest. A verifier, registry policy, or later Lab 8 Cosign verification step would check the signed version of this statement to connect the image digest to the SBOM. It does not prove that the image is safe, that every vulnerability is fixed, or that the SBOM is complete; it only packages the claim that this SBOM belongs to that exact image digest.
